title: Channel Duality and Midpoint Invariance in Random Walks with Resetting
summary: We study absorption of a biased nearest-neighbor random walk on a finite interval that is reset to its initial position. The central contribution is an exact duality between the two absorption channels, which holds mode by mode in the spectral representation and step by step in time, together with the invariance it produces: when the interval has even length, the ruin probability from its midpoint equals the classical reset-free value for every law of the reset times independent of the walk, provided absorption occurs almost surely.
